context:
This is a mechanical default-flip across four locations plus a small
logic addition to `_existing_obt()` for a stale-file log message. No new
code paths, no new dependencies. The transformer already emits parquet
when asked.

Work order: w1 first (the actual flip), then w2 (UX improvement for
stale-file detection), then w3 (tests catch any accidental regression),
then w4 (docs), then w5 (end-to-end smoke).

Reference existing parquet path: `etl/transformer.py:730` already emits
`COPY ... TO '...' (FORMAT PARQUET)`. No changes needed to the export
logic itself.
description:
TPC-DS OBT currently defaults to pipe-delimited `.dat` output. At SF1 this
produces an 11GB uncompressed file (5,041,336 rows × 518 columns). The
schema is intentionally wide (One Big Table) - that is not a bug - but
`.dat` is a pathological storage choice for a 518-column table where:

- Every row carries ~300-400 NULL columns (store rows have NULL for all
  web_site_*, web_page_*, call_center_*, catalog_page_* columns; web rows
  are NULL for all store_* and call_center_* columns; etc.)
- Many dimension attributes repeat textual values (customer names,
  addresses, product descriptions) that compress trivially column-wise
- DataFrame platforms (DataFusion, Polars, Pandas) cannot practically
  load 11GB of pipe-delimited text into memory at SF1

Parquet's columnar encoding with null suppression and per-column
compression is expected to reduce the file materially - an order-of-
magnitude shrink is plausible given the null density and text repetition,
but the actual ratio is validated in w5. The transformer already
supports parquet output - the export
branch at `etl/transformer.py:730` emits parquet when
`output_format="parquet"` is passed. What is missing is making parquet
the default so DataFrame platforms work out of the box and SQL platforms
get a much smaller artifact for free.

This change:
- Flips the default `output_format` from `"dat"` to `"parquet"` in four
  places (benchmark `__init__`, `generate_data()`, `BenchmarkOptionSpec`,
  transformer `transform()`).
- Updates `_existing_obt()` to detect parquet first and trigger
  regeneration when only a stale `.dat` exists (it will not auto-delete).
- Keeps `.dat` available via explicit `--benchmark-option output_format=dat`
  so anyone reproducing older results or benchmarking a platform that
  cannot read parquet still has a path.

Downstream impact: DuckDB, ClickHouse, DataFusion-SQL, and all DataFrame
platforms read parquet natively via their existing CSV/parquet auto-detect
loaders. No platform-side code changes are expected. SQL platforms that
generate DDL first and then `COPY` from file will benefit from the smaller
artifact and faster load times.
